content: Tolnaftate is a medication that inhibits the growth of fungi responsible for skin infections such as athlete's foot, jock itch, and ringworm. It may also be prescribed for other conditions; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Tolnaftate is available in various forms, including cream, liquid, powder, gel, spray powder, and spray liquid, all intended for application to the skin. It is typically applied twice daily. Follow the instructions on the packaging or prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it, or apply it more frequently than prescribed. Symptoms such as burning and soreness from athlete's foot or itching from jock itch should improve within 2–3 days. However, continue treatment for at least 2 weeks after symptoms disappear. A full course of treatment may last 4–6 weeks. Before applying the medication, thoroughly clean the affected area, allow it to dry, and gently rub the medication into the skin until most of it is absorbed. Use only enough medication to cover the affected area. Wash your hands after application. For spray and powder forms, apply them between the toes, and lightly treat socks and shoes. Shake sprays well before each use, and spray from a distance of at least 6 inches. Before using tolnaftate, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to tolnaftate or any other medications. Also, disclose any prescription or nonprescription medications, including vitamins, that you are currently taking. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while using tolnaftate, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Tolnaftate may cause side effects. If you experience skin irritation, contact your doctor immediately. For serious side effects, you or your doctor may report them to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store tolnaftate in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Do not puncture spray cans or dispose of them in fire. Discard any expired or unused medication. Consult your pharmacist for proper disposal methods. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Tolnaftate is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not swallow it. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin medications to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist. If your symptoms persist after completing the course of tolnaftate, contact your doctor.
